study_identification_part.si4_title: Brain-Charting Autism and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Reveals Distinct and Overlapping Neurobiology

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states both research hypotheses/questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling. The abstract and introduction explicitly describe the study objectives: to characterize cortical anatomy associated with autism and ADHD using population modeling (normative modeling) benchmarked against models of average brain development. The study examines sex and age differences, relationships with autistic traits, and co-occurrence of autism and ADHD. The purpose of applying normative modeling is described as providing a unified framework for studying age-specific and sex-specific divergences in brain development, contextualizing alterations in light of typical brain development, and addressing heterogeneity in these conditions.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Here, we used population modeling and a large, multisite neuroimaging dataset (N = 4255 after quality control) to characterize cortical anatomy associated with autism and ADHD, benchmarked against models of average brain development based on a sample of more than 75,000 individuals. We also examined sex and age differences and relationship with autistic traits and explored the co-occurrence of autism and ADHD... Population modeling, often referred to as normative modeling, provides a unified framework for studying age-specific and sex-specific divergences in brain development... Critically, these alterations must be contextualized in light of typical brain development given the neurodevelopmental nature of autism and ADHD... Here, we leveraged models of average brain development previously characterized by our group (98) to quantify alterations related to autism and ADHD.

nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: T1 images from each dataset were processed using FreeSurfer, version 6.0.1 (105). Regional estimates of each cortical measure were extracted based on the Desikan-Killiany atlas (106)... All scans underwent manual QC of raw image and FreeSurfer surface reconstructions using our FSQC tool (107), which allows for the evaluation of both surface reconstruction and raw scan quality, including motion artifacts (108). A cutoff of 2.5 was used for FSQC (107). Because even small variations in quality can bias downstream analyses (108,109), we also included the FreeSurfer-derived Euler number (110) as a covariate in all analyses.

The meaning and direction of deviation scores are explained: centile scores range from 0 to 1, with 0.5 representing the average of the reference sample; positive effect sizes indicate autism/ADHD > control group (higher centiles), and negative effect sizes indicate autism/ADHD < control group (lower centiles). Quantitative thresholds are reported: the study examines 'extreme' centile scores using percentile-based cutoffs in supplementary analyses, and statistical significance is determined using false discovery rate correction (5% FDR). Clinical implications of deviation patterns are discussed extensively, including relationships with symptoms, sex and age modulation effects, comparison to group-level findings, heterogeneity and individualized patterns, and limitations of interpretation. The discussion contextualizes findings in relation to previous literature and notes the small effect sizes may limit clinical significance.
